title: Synchronous hepatocellular carcinoma and IPNB-associated intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma in a patient with resolved viral hepatitis: a case report of diagnostic pitfall and margin-negative resection
abstract: Background Synchronous hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct (IPNB)-associated intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) is a rare dual-lineage hepatobiliary malignancy. Although radical resection for conventional synchronous HCC and ICC has been well documented, reported experience with margin-negative (R0) resection for this specific tumor complex remains scarce. Case Summary A 77-year-old male with resolved hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection and hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection with sustained virological response (SVR) presented with intermittent right upper quadrant pain, abdominal distension, scleral icterus, pruritus, nausea, and vomiting. Imaging studies revealed multifocal hepatic lesions and a biliary tract mass, and he was initially misdiagnosed as metastatic cholangiocarcinoma. Staging laparoscopy confirmed resectability, followed by open margin-negative resection. Intraoperative cholangioscopy and frozen-section analysis identified a pedunculated IPNB arising from the right hepatic duct and confirmed negative bile duct margins. Final pathology confirmed well-differentiated HCC and a separate high-grade IPNB with associated moderately to poorly differentiated ICC. The HCC and biliary lesion were separated by non-neoplastic parenchyma without a transition between them, excluding combined hepatocellular-cholangiocarcinoma (cHCC-CCA). Regional lymph nodes were not removed or histologically examined (pNx for both tumors). Margins exceeded 1 cm for both components. The patient recovered uneventfully; at 3-month follow-up, tumor markers were normal with no radiological recurrence. Conclusion This report presents a rare case of margin-negative (R0) resection with unassessed nodal status (pNx) for synchronous HCC and IPNB-associated ICC in a patient with resolved HBV infection and HCV infection with SVR. The coexistence of multifocal hepatic lesions with a biliary tract mass should not be presumed to indicate metastatic disease; in this case, surgical exploration with intraoperative frozen-section analysis and cholangioscopy was useful for diagnosis and management, with the 3-month follow-up documenting only an early postoperative outcome.

title: Impact of hepatitis delta virus infection on waiting list outcomes: A competing-risks analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND Liver transplantation is the gold standard for end-stage liver disease, but the shortage of donor organs results in extended waiting lists and considerable mortality before a graft becomes available. Model for end-stage liver disease (MELD)-based allocation has reduced waiting-list mortality and shortened waiting times across many national programs, but its predictive accuracy is not uniform. Hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection promotes faster progression of fibrosis and leads to earlier decompensation. Whether HDV status provides independent prognostic information beyond the MELD score in predicting waiting-list outcomes remains insufficiently investigated. AIM To assess the impact of hepatitis delta infection on waiting-list outcomes through a competing-risks analysis. METHODS We conducted an ambispective national cohort study of adults listed for liver transplantation (1 January 2013-31 December 2025). The retrospective phase covered 2013-2017 and the prospective phase 2018-2025. Two separate etiologic analyses were performed, comparing HDV infection first with hepatitis B virus (HBV) monoinfection and then with non-delta viral infection, comprising HBV monoinfection, HBV/hepatitis C virus (HCV) coinfection, and HCV monoinfection. Death on the waiting list and transplantation were treated as competing events. Cumulative incidence functions (CIF) were estimated using the Aalen-Johansen method. Multivariable cause-specific Cox and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models were fitted for death and for transplantation. RESULTS Of 313 adults, 174 (55.6%) had delta infection. The delta group had a more advanced baseline profile. The 5-year CIF of waiting-list death did not differ between the delta and non-delta viral groups (45.9% vs 42.9%; Gray’s test, P = 0.696), whereas transplantation was more frequent in the delta group (43.1% vs 21.7%; P = 0.001). In cause-specific models for the viral cohort, HDV approximately doubled the hazard of both waiting-list death [cause-specific hazard ratio (csHR) = 2.12, 95%CI: 1.38-3.24, P CONCLUSION HDV increased the cause-specific hazard of waiting-list death, but this effect was attenuated by more frequent transplantation. HDV status may aid risk stratification in endemic settings, although current evidence is insufficient to justify a formal MELD exception.

title: Development and Validation of a Nomogram to Predict Recompensation in Patients With HBV-Related Acute-on-Chronic Liver Failure: A Multicenter Retrospective Study.
abstract: ABSTRACT Limited studies have investigated the predictors of hepatic recompensation in patients with hepatitis B virus (HBV)‐related acute‐on‐chronic liver failure (ACLF). Establishing a clinically applicable predictive model for recompensation in ACLF patients is of critical importance. A total of 304 HBV‐ACLF patients were included in the study, 169 patients as training cohort and 135 patients as validation cohort. In the training cohort, 72 patients (42.6%) achieved recompensation within the first year following an ACLF episode, whereas 87 patients (64.4%) in the validation cohort achieved recompensation during the same period. Age, alpha‐fetoprotein, total bilirubin, white blood cell count, hepatic encephalopathy, and gastrointestinal bleeding were selected for inclusion in the model. The nomogram demonstrated excellent discriminative ability, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.842 (95% CI: 0.784–0.900) in the training cohort and 0.855 (95% CI: 0.785–0.926) in the validation cohort. Calibration curves showed strong agreement between predicted and observed recompensation rates. DCA further confirmed the model's clinical utility for decision‐making. This model demonstrated superior predictive performance compared to the MELD score, MELD‐Na score, and MELD 3.0 score. The developed nomogram provides an accurate and clinically applicable tool for predicting recompensation likelihood, enhancing personalized management of HBV‐ACLF patients.

title: Hepatitis E in suspected acute hepatitis cases in Brazil: A comparison with hepatitis A.
abstract: Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is an underrecognized cause of acute viral hepatitis worldwide, with growing public health relevance, particularly in settings where routine diagnostic testing is limited. Hepatitis A virus (HAV) is another epidemiologically related hepatitis virus, but few studies have directly compared these infections in Brazil. This study aimed to (1) determine the frequency of acute hepatitis E (AHE) and evaluate the contribution of HEV infection to the burden of hepatitis among patients with suspected acute disease attended in public healthcare institutions in Brazil; (2) assess the prevalence of acquired immunity to HEV and HAV; and (3) compare demographic characteristics, risk factors, and clinical-laboratory findings associated with HEV and HAV infections. We enrolled 1,721 adults (≥18 years) with suspected acute hepatitis from 16 Brazilian states between October 2019 and May 2023. Serum samples were tested for anti-HEV IgG/IgM and anti-HAV IgG/IgM by immunoassay and for HEV and HAV RNA by RT-PCR. Demographic, behavioral, clinical, and laboratory data were collected using a standardized questionnaire. Group comparisons were performed using univariate analyses and logistic regression, with statistical significance set at p < 0.05. Anti-HEV IgG was detected in 89 individuals (5.2%), whereas anti-HAV IgG was detected in 1,352 (78.6%). Anti-HEV IgG seroprevalence was higher in the South, Southeast, and Central West regions and among heterosexuals, and it increased with age, reaching 13.0% among individuals aged ≥65 years. Seropositivity was associated with markers of previous exposure or immunity, including HAV, HBV, Leptospira, and Toxoplasma. A total of 124 acute hepatitis cases were identified: 16 (12.9%) AHE and 108 (87.1%) acute hepatitis A (AHA). Compared with AHA cases, AHE cases occurred in older individuals and were more frequent among women and heterosexual participants. All AHA cases occurred in urban areas, whereas AHE cases were observed in both urban and rural settings. AHA cases showed higher aminotransferase levels and more frequent jaundice than AHE cases. HEV accounts for a small but distinct proportion of suspected acute hepatitis cases in Brazil and shows epidemiological and clinical characteristics that differ from HAV. Incorporating HEV testing into routine diagnostic algorithms may improve etiological clarification and surveillance of acute hepatitis.
authors: Denize Ornelas Pereira Salvador de Oliveira
Ana Catharina de Seixas Santos Nastri

title: Systems Pharmacology of Human Oncoviruses: Network-Based Drug Discovery for Virus-Driven Cancers.
abstract: Human oncoviruses, including high-risk HPV, EBV, HBV, HCV, MCPyV, KSHV, and HTLV-1, account for approximately 15%-20% of global human malignancies. Rather than acting through isolated pathways, viral oncoproteins systematically rewire host regulatory networks, rendering conventional single-target oncology paradigms vulnerable to rapid resistance and clinical failure. Systems pharmacology offers a transformative, network-centric framework that views virus-driven cancers as systemic perturbations of host protein-protein interaction networks. This review synthesises computational methodology, network topology, and drug discovery strategies across major human oncoviruses. We examine how graph centrality algorithms, quantitative network proximity metrics (Z-score), and complementary exposure synergy modelling (S AB ) uncover hidden network vulnerabilities and guide targeted drug repurposing. Despite distinct genomic structures and tissue tropisms, oncogenic viruses converge on shared host interactome hubs, notably TP53, AKT1, BCL2, MYC, STAT3, and VEGFA, to drive cell cycle dysregulation, apoptotic suppression, and microenvironmental remodelling. We evaluate repositioned synthetic pharmaceuticals (such as kinase inhibitors and host ion channel blockers) and multi-target bioactive formulations, detailing their mechanisms in targeting viral host dependencies. Finally, we address key translational bottlenecks, including disparities between in silico binding predictions and in vivo pharmacokinetics, extensive plasma protein binding, tumour penetration barriers, and viral latency reservoirs. Overcoming these hurdles will require integrating deep graph learning, single-cell spatial multi-omics, and patient-derived organoid models to accelerate the clinical realization of network-targeted therapies in viral oncology.

title: Modulation of the FAK-Src Signalling Axis by Oncoviruses: Molecular Mechanisms, Functional Consequences, and Therapeutic Opportunities.
abstract: Oncoviruses play a role in cellular transformation and cancer progression by manipulating host signalling pathways, such as the FAK-Src axis. Preclinical evidence suggests that viral proteins can modulate this axis through direct interactions, integrin signalling, tumour suppressor inactivation, transcriptional and kinase reprogramming, calcium/ROS signalling, regulation of phosphatases, and epigenetic modifications. Important examples include HPV E2 and E6/E7, EBV LMP1 and LMP2A, HBV HBx, HCV Core and E2, and KSHV proteins. FAK-Src disruption can activate pathways such as PI3K/AKT, Rho GTPase, AP-1, and NF-κB, thereby enhancing migration, invasion, survival, angiogenesis, and modulation of the immune response. In some infections, this axis may also be involved at different stages of the viral life cycle. This review examines the molecular mechanisms of FAK-Src regulation by oncoviruses and its functional and therapeutic implications. It also reviews FAK/Src targeting strategies, distinguishing experimental inhibitors, multitargeted agents, and compounds under clinical evaluation, emphasising the limited clinical evidence specific to each virus. Finally, pFAK and pSrc are reviewed as potential markers of pathway activation and pharmacodynamic interaction with the target; however, current evidence is insufficient for their use as valid diagnostic or predictive biomarkers. A better understanding of the virus-host-FAK/Src interaction could help develop mechanism-based therapeutic approaches and biomarker-based patient selection.

In some infections, this axis may also be involved at different stages of the viral life cycle. This review examines the molecular mechanisms of FAK-Src regulation by oncoviruses and its functional and therapeutic implications. It also reviews FAK/Src targeting strategies, distinguishing experimental inhibitors, multitargeted agents, and compounds under clinical evaluation, emphasising the limited clinical evidence specific to each virus. Finally, pFAK and pSrc are reviewed as potential markers of pathway activation and pharmacodynamic interaction with the target; however, current evidence is insufficient for their use as valid diagnostic or predictive biomarkers. A better understanding of the virus-host-FAK/Src interaction could help develop mechanism-based therapeutic approaches and biomarker-based patient selection.

title: Vaccines for Cancer: A Translational Science Review.
abstract: IMPORTANCE: Advances in tumor immunology and vaccine technology are reshaping cancer vaccine development after decades of limited clinical success. More than 2000 immunogenic tumor proteins or antigens have been identified, the types of immune responses required for tumor eradication have been defined, and safe and effective vaccine delivery technologies have been developed. This progress has renewed clinical investigation of cancer vaccines for multiple types of cancer. OBSERVATIONS: Vaccines, such as those against human papillomavirus and hepatitis B, are composed of (1) an antigen target, (2) an adjuvant to activate the immune system, and (3) a vaccine delivery vehicle. Antigens can be derived from tumor mutations termed neoantigens, or cancer-associated nonmutated proteins, which are normal human proteins that are abnormally expressed in cancer. The tumor can also act as an antigen source, such as when immunization occurs with whole tumor cells or by directly injecting an immunogenic substance into the tumor to elicit an adaptive immune response. T and B lymphocytes, cells of the adaptive immune system, are stimulated by cancer vaccines and can provide a highly specific and durable immune response directed against cancer. Vaccines that elicit adaptive immunity are approved for cancer treatment. Sipuleucel-T, a vaccine against the antigen prostatic acid phosphatase, reduced all-cause mortality compared with placebo in men with metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer (32% vs 23%; hazard ratio, 0.78 [95% CI, 0.61-0.98]; P = .03). Compared with granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor, a systemic immune stimulant, talimogene laherparepvec increased rates of a 6-month or longer complete or partial response, defined as the disappearance of all treated disease and at least a 50% decrease in the sum of the products of perpendicular diameters of the measurable lesion with no new lesions, respectively, when injected into advanced melanoma lesions (16.3% [95% CI, 12.1%-20.5%] vs 2.1% [95% CI, 0%-4.5%]; odds ratio, 8.9; P < .001). Most cancer vaccines have mild adverse effects, such as fatigue, fever, and injection site reactions. Combining cancer vaccines with chemotherapy or immunotherapy can increase the magnitude of the immune response and potentially result in greater reduction in cancer size. Combining the personalized mutation-based messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccine (mRNA-4157) with the immune checkpoint inhibitor pembrolizumab for resected high-risk stage IIIB to IV cutaneous melanoma improved relapse-free survival compared with pembrolizumab alone (76.6% vs 60%; hazard ratio, 0.56 [95% CI, 0.31-1.02]; P = .05). Cancer vaccines are undergoing evaluation in clinical trials to prevent cancer recurrence and for primary cancer prevention. CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Cancer vaccines can treat several types of malignant neoplasms, including melanoma, prostate cancer, and bladder cancer. Adverse effects associated with cancer vaccines are generally mild and of short duration, promoting eventual integration of vaccination into treatment regimens with chemotherapy and immunotherapy. Cancer vaccines are increasingly undergoing evaluation for primary prevention.

title: Systematic STI screening in unaccompanied migrant minors: a 6-year experience with urine-based NAAT.
abstract: UNLABELLED: Systematic screening for sexually transmitted infections (STI), beyond serology, is not standard in arrival protocols for unaccompanied migrant minors (UMM). In 2020, our center incorporated urine-based nucleic acid amplification tests (NAAT)-based screening into the existing serology-based protocol (HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B/C), and we describe the additional diagnoses of STI identified through NAAT. We conducted a retrospective observational descriptive study (2020-2025) of 226 UMM (99.6% male) in Madrid undergoing serological screening for HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B and C, with additional urine-based multiplex PCR (NAAT) screening for STI. Urine-based NAAT, performed in 163/226 participants (72.1%), identified six positive cases (3.7%, 95% CI 1.4-7.8%) of C. genitalium, or Ureaplasma spp. Of these, four patients (2.5%, 95% CI 0.7-6.2%) had actionable infections that were treated. Serology identified no HIV (0/218) or hepatitis C cases (0/212), one syphilis case (0.5%, 95% CI 0.0-2.6%, 1/209), and three chronic hepatitis B cases (1.4%, 95% CI 0.3-3.9%, 3/221). None of the cases had symptoms recorded. CONCLUSION: Urine NAAT identified six infections (four actionable) not detectable by serology. However, three of eight patients with actionable infections were lost to follow-up, highlighting that the benefit of systematic screening depends on strengthening linkage-to-care alongside testing. WHAT IS KNOWN: • Serological screening (HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B/C) is standard in arrival health assessments for unaccompanied migrant minors, but systematic STI screening beyond serology is not routinely protocoled. • Systematic screening is especially valuable in this population, as follow-up is often limited by care fragmentation and transfers between reception centers. WHAT IS NEW: • Urine-based NAAT screening identified additional STI in patients with no symptoms recorded, that were not detectable by serology alone.

title: Bictegravir/Lenacapavir: A 2-Drug Regimen for the Treatment of HIV-1 Infection.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of bictegravir/lenacapavir for the treatment of HIV-1 infection. DATA SOURCES: A literature search was conducted in PubMed and Google Scholar (January 2016-August 2026) using the search terms bictegravir and lenacapavir. Other data sources included abstracts presented at recent conferences and the prescribing information. STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: All English-language studies assessing the efficacy and safety of bictegravir/lenacapavir for the treatment of HIV-1 infection were considered for inclusion. DATA SYNTHESIS: Bictegravir is an established second-generation integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI), whereas lenacapavir is a novel capsid inhibitor. Both antiretrovirals are highly active against HIV-1. Bictegravir/lenacapavir 75 mg/50 mg was shown to be safe and effective in two phase 3 clinical trials after switching from complex antiretroviral therapy (ART) or bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide. The Food and Drug Administration approved this combination for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in adults who are virologically suppressed on stable ART with no resistance to the individual components. It is available as a single-tablet regimen (STR) taken orally once daily.Relevance to Patient Care and Clinical Practice in Comparison With Existing Drugs:Bictegravir/lenacapvir is the first INSTI-capsid inhibitor 2-drug STR indicated for the treatment of HIV-1 infection. The combination could be useful for patients who want to simplify their regimen and/or those who cannot use a nucleos(t)ide or a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor. It is not active against hepatitis B virus coinfection. CONCLUSIONS: Bictegravir/lenacapvir is safe and efficacious as a 2-drug regimen for the treatment of adults with HIV-1 infection.

title: ARBITER: retrieval-augmented generation for automated PROBAST+AI risk-of-bias assessment of HIV, HBV and HCV prediction models: a proof-of-concept validation study
abstract: Abstract Clinical prediction models for blood-borne virus infections — HIV, hepatitis B (HBV), and hepatitis C (HCV) — are published widely, yet appraising their quality remains labour-intensive and inconsistently applied. We developed the Automated Risk-of-Bias Inspection Tool for Evidence Review (ARBITER) to characterise studies, separate model-development and model-evaluation pathways, and generate a categorical judgment with verbatim supporting evidence from manuscript text for each PROBAST+AI signalling question. We illustrate the application of ARBITER (using the Google Gemini 2.5 Pro API) to ten prediction model studies for HIV, HBV and HCV, comparing its accuracy against Claude Sonnet 4.6 (via its chat interface) and a human statistical expert; one study (Kerschberger 2021) informed pipeline refinement before assessment of the remaining nine. title: Enteric infections as HIV indicator conditions for HIV testing: An umbrella review.
abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this umbrella review was to explore whether faeco-oral sexually transmissible enteric infections should be indicator conditions for HIV testing. METHOD: Four bibliographical databases (Medline, Emcare, Embase, CINAHL) were searched in May 2026 for systematic reviews written in English, exploring HIV in people with faeco-oral sexually transmissible enteric infections. Two authors independently reviewed full-text publications, assessed risk of bias (Joanna Briggs toolkit) and performed a narrative synthesis to identify characteristics relevant to HIV indicator condition testing. Results were reported using the PRIOR guidelines and the review was registered on PROSPERO (ID:CRD420261387222). RESULTS: There were 15 manuscripts in this umbrella review, all of which included study populations consisting exclusively of men who have sex with men (MSM). There were 10 032 MSM across 207 manuscripts that explored Shigella spp., Campylobacter spp., diarrhoeagenic E. coli, Salmonella spp., Giardia duodenalis, Entamoeba histolytica, Hepatitis A, Cryptosporidium spp., hepatitis E, Strongyloides stercoralis, Enterobius vermicularis, intestinal spirochaetosis (Brachyspiraspp.), Blastocystis spp. and enteric viruses. Living with HIV was observed in MSM with all enteric infections. Having a new diagnosis of HIV was seen in MSM with hepatitis A. Having Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, syphilis and other (or previous) sexually transmitted infections (STI); visiting sex on premises venues, and engaging in chemsex were also observed in MSM with enteric infections. CONCLUSION: These data provide the best evidence to date that faeco-oral sexually transmissible enteric infections in MSM are indicator diseases for HIV testing and testing for syphilis, hepatitis B and C and other STIs.

title: Prevalence of blood-borne infections and associated risk factors among users of performance-enhancing substances: A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: The use of performance-enhancing substances (PES) has expanded beyond elite sport and is increasingly prevalent among recreational gym-goers, some of whom engage in behaviors that may increase the risk of blood-borne virus transmission. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to synthesize evidence on the prevalence of HIV, HBV, and HCV among PES users, quantitatively estimate prevalence where comparable laboratory-confirmed data were available, and identify behavioral and contextual factors associated with infection risk. A systematic search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, and the review was reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020. Random-effects meta-analyses of sufficiently comparable laboratory-confirmed prevalence data were conducted using binomial-normal generalized linear mixed models with a logit link, while remaining evidence was synthesized narratively. Twenty-one studies met the inclusion criteria. Pooled prevalence was 0.75% (95% CI: <0.01–9.63%) for HIV, 5.60% (95% CI: 1.71–15.16%) for HBV based on anti-HBc, and 4.33% (95% CI: 1.47–9.34%) for HCV based on anti-HCV. These estimates were based on few independent studies and should therefore be interpreted cautiously. Higher HIV prevalence was reported in self-reported data from higher-risk subpopulations, particularly men who have sex with men. Key risk-related factors included sharing or reusing injection equipment, concomitant injection of psychoactive substances, risky sexual behaviors, and a history of incarceration. Low uptake of viral testing and HBV vaccination was also reported. These findings highlight the need for targeted harm-reduction, testing, vaccination, and education strategies for PES users, while further research using standardized diagnostic and reporting methods is needed to strengthen prevalence estimates.

title: Label-Free Nucleic Acid Amplification in a Self-regulated All-Fiber Photothermal Microcavity.
abstract: Nucleic acid amplification commonly relies on fluorescent labels and electrically driven thermal control, limiting simplicity, scalability, and remote deployment. Here, we establish a label-free optical strategy based on amplification-associated refractive-index (RI) evolution within a confined optothermal microcavity. During amplification, the accumulation of nucleic acid products alters the composition and molecular polarizability of the reaction medium, contributing to a progressive increase in its effective RI. This bulk RI change is converted into interferometric phase accumulation under thermally stabilized conditions, enabling real-time optical readout without labels. We implement this strategy in a 0.94 nL fiber Fabry-Perot microcavity that integrates localized optothermal regulation and phase-sensitive interrogation within a single optical pathway. The confined geometry enables rapid optothermal heating, reaching a 1 °C temperature rise in 15 ms, nearly three orders of magnitude faster than conventional electrical heating. Using hepatitis B virus (HBV) DNA as a model target, we achieve a detection limit of 5.24 copies/nL and quantitative agreement with fluorescence-based assays, while isothermal amplification reduces the total assay time by approximately 50% relative to commercial qPCR. Frequency-division multiplexing enables parallel multi-target analysis, while stable transmission is maintained over 20 km fiber links. Our results establish amplification-associated RI evolution as a promising label-free transduction mechanism for fiber-integrated molecular diagnostics.

title: Determinants of disease in Italian patients at the time of their first diagnosis of liver cirrhosis
abstract: Abstract Background : The epidemiology, etiologies and clinical presentation of cirrhosis have changed markedly in recent years; however, national-level data remain limited. Aims: To describe the epidemiological profile and metabolic and non-metabolic determinants of cirrhosis in Italy in 2024. Patients and methods: In this cross-sectional, multicentre observational study, 1195 consecutive patients with cirrhosis were enrolled from 11 tertiary hepatology centres across Italy. Eligible participants had a new diagnosis of previously unknown cirrhosis or a previous diagnosis with first evaluation at a participating centre in 2024. Demographic, socioeconomic, etiological, clinical and laboratory data were collected. Metabolic and non-metabolic determinants of cirrhosis were ranked by prevalence using Pareto chart analysis. Results: Among 1195 patients, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) was the most prevalent etiology (321 patients, 26.9%), followed by alcohol-related liver disease (ALD) (269, 22.5%), viral etiologies (263, 22.0%) and other causes (116, 9.7%). Mixed etiologies were identified in 226 patients (18.9%), including Met-ALD, Met-virus, ALD-virus, Met-ALD-virus and PBC-AIH overlap. In the Pareto analysis, arterial hypertension ranked first, followed by type 2 diabetes mellitus, obesity, HCV infection, alcohol abuse and HBV infection. Despite the growing metabolic burden, viral hepatitis remained a major contributor, accounting for 28% of etiologies (137/490) among patients with a previous diagnosis of cirrhosis. Conclusions: Cirrhosis epidemiology in Italy is shifting toward metabolic predominance, with MASLD emerging as the leading etiology. Nevertheless, viral hepatitis remains a substantial contributor. The frequent overlap of etiologies highlights the increasing complexity of cirrhosis management.

Patients and methods: In this cross-sectional, multicentre observational study, 1195 consecutive patients with cirrhosis were enrolled from 11 tertiary hepatology centres across Italy. Eligible participants had a new diagnosis of previously unknown cirrhosis or a previous diagnosis with first evaluation at a participating centre in 2024. Demographic, socioeconomic, etiological, clinical and laboratory data were collected. Metabolic and non-metabolic determinants of cirrhosis were ranked by prevalence using Pareto chart analysis. Results: Among 1195 patients, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) was the most prevalent etiology (321 patients, 26.9%), followed by alcohol-related liver disease (ALD) (269, 22.5%), viral etiologies (263, 22.0%) and other causes (116, 9.7%). Mixed etiologies were identified in 226 patients (18.9%), including Met-ALD, Met-virus, ALD-virus, Met-ALD-virus and PBC-AIH overlap. In the Pareto analysis, arterial hypertension ranked first, followed by type 2 diabetes mellitus, obesity, HCV infection, alcohol abuse and HBV infection. Despite the growing metabolic burden, viral hepatitis remained a major contributor, accounting for 28% of etiologies (137/490) among patients with a previous diagnosis of cirrhosis. Conclusions: Cirrhosis epidemiology in Italy is shifting toward metabolic predominance, with MASLD emerging as the leading etiology. Nevertheless, viral hepatitis remains a substantial contributor. The frequent overlap of etiologies highlights the increasing complexity of cirrhosis management.

title: The aMAP Score Effectively Stratifies Hepatocellular Carcinoma Risk in the Steatotic Liver Disease Population.
abstract: BACKGROUND & AIMS: Steatotic liver disease (SLD) is an increasingly important cause of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), yet validated risk stratification tools remain limited. We aim to evaluate the aMAP score, initially developed for HCC risk prediction mainly in viral hepatitis across international cohorts, in the SLD population. METHODS: 156 406 SLD participants were included from the UK Biobank (UKB) and 3166 SLD patients with virally suppressed chronic hepatitis B from a Chinese cohort. The predictive and stratification performance of the aMAP score was assessed and compared with the PAGE-B, mPAGE-B, CAMD and MASLD-HCC scores. A refined stratification of the aMAP-defined high-risk population identified a subgroup exceeding the recommended surveillance threshold. RESULTS: Median follow-up was 13.64 years in UKB and 9.97 years in the Chinese cohort, with 287 and 58 patients developing HCC, respectively. The aMAP score showed favourable discrimination (C-indices: 0.80 [95% CI, 0.78-0.83] in UKB; 0.79 [95% CI, 0.73-0.85] in the Chinese cohort). The 15-year cumulative HCC incidence by aMAP in UKB was 0.06% (95% CI, 0.04%-0.08%), 0.26% (95% CI, 0.21%-0.31%) and 1.43% (95% CI, 1.14%-1.72%) for low-, intermediate- and high-risk groups (high vs. low risk, sHR: 28.51; 95% CI, 19.58-41.52; Gray's test p 64) identified a very-high-risk subgroup in UKB with 15-year cumulative incidences of 3.08% (training; 95% CI, 1.29%-4.87%) and 5.35% (validation; 95% CI, 3.04%-7.67%). CONCLUSIONS: The aMAP score is an effective tool for HCC risk stratification among SLD patients. The refined aMAP threshold accurately identifies very-high-risk patients qualifying for guideline-recommended surveillance.

title: Research progress on molecular markers related to diagnosis and prognosis and anti-hepatocellular carcinoma signaling pathways
abstract: Abstract Objective Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) boasts high global incidence and mortality. Severe HBV infection and prevalent non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) lead to a heavy HCC disease burden in China. HCC has occult early symptoms, and most patients are diagnosed at advanced stages with high postoperative recurrence risk. Traditional imaging and serological markers fail to achieve accurate early diagnosis and identify residual tumors, unable to meet the clinical needs of precise and individualized HCC treatment. This study systematically reviewed HCC diagnostic and prognostic molecular markers, analyzed the defects of traditional markers, illustrated the mechanisms and clinical efficacy of novel markers, sorted out anti-HCC core signaling pathways, and explored multi-marker combined strategies to support precise HCC diagnosis and treatment. Methods We integrated up-to-date domestic and international omics data, cellular and animal experimental verification results, and clinical evidence. This study analyzed the clinical and molecular deficiencies of traditional serological markers, clarified the expression features, regulatory pathways and translational potential of novel molecular markers, explored abnormal mechanisms and drug targets of key HCC signaling pathways, and established an optimization and evaluation system for multi-marker combined detection. Result Traditional HCC molecular markers have poor sensitivity and specificity, and cannot distinguish postoperative tissue repair from residual tumors, with weak correlation with HCC biological behaviors. Novel markers including oncogene (Onc) and tumor suppressor genes (TSGs), non-coding RNAs, translation initiation- and protein homeostasis-related genes and metabolic reprogramming-related genes are abnormally expressed in HCC. They regulate tumor proliferation, apoptosis, invasion and metastasis, improving early diagnosis, prognostic stratification and recurrence warning. Multi-marker combination compensates for single detection defects, and pathway-targeted drugs optimize the accuracy of HCC prognosis and individualized treatment formulation. Conclusion With the advantages of non-invasive detection and dynamic reflection of tumor characteristics, molecular markers combined with pathway-targeted therapy can break the bottlenecks of traditional HCC diagnosis and treatment. The synergism of traditional and novel markers, multi-marker joint detection and targeted therapy has great clinical translational value, providing a new direction for realizing precise diagnosis, prognosis and individualized treatment of HCC. The summarized mechanisms and strategies can support the clinical practice of HCC precision medicine.

title: HEPLISAV-B Breaks Immune Tolerance and Induces HBV Control via CD4 T Cell-Dependent Mechanism in Chronic HBV Mouse Model
abstract: Background: Chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection (CHB) affects nearly 300 million individuals globally and remains incurable with current antiviral therapies, which suppress viral replication but rarely achieve a functional cure, defined by sustained loss of hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg). CHB is characterized by profound virus-induced immune tolerance that limits the efficacy of conventional therapeutic vaccination strategies. Objective: To evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and immunological mechanisms of HEPLISAV-B, a CpG-1018 adjuvanted HBsAg vaccine, in breaking immune tolerance and inducing functional cure-like responses in a murine model of CHB. Design: Using the adeno-associated virus-HBV (AAV-HBV) mouse model, mice with high levels of persistent HBV viremia were vaccinated with two doses of HEPLISAV-B. Virological outcomes in the blood and liver, immune responses and mechanisms were assessed. Results: HEPLISAV-B induced rapid and durable HBsAg clearance, markedly reduced circulating and intrahepatic HBV DNA and RNA, and suppressed viral replication without hepatocellular injury. Vaccination elicited robust, sustained anti-HBs IgG1 and IgA responses, enhanced HBsAg-specific T- and B-cell immunity, reduced CD4 regulatory T cells, and decreased PD-1 expression on CD4 T cells. Therapeutic efficacy was strictly dependent on CD4 T cells and the CD40/CD40L signaling pathway, but independent of CD8 T cells, indicating a CD4-driven, non-cytolytic antiviral mechanism critical for HEPLISAV-B-induced HBV control. Conclusions: HEPLISAV-B effectively breaks HBV-induced immune tolerance and restores coordinated antiviral immunity through a CD4 T cell/CD40L-dependent pathway. The findings support its potential as a therapeutic vaccine in CHB patients.

Objective: To evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and immunological mechanisms of HEPLISAV-B, a CpG-1018 adjuvanted HBsAg vaccine, in breaking immune tolerance and inducing functional cure-like responses in a murine model of CHB. Design: Using the adeno-associated virus-HBV (AAV-HBV) mouse model, mice with high levels of persistent HBV viremia were vaccinated with two doses of HEPLISAV-B. Virological outcomes in the blood and liver, immune responses and mechanisms were assessed. Results: HEPLISAV-B induced rapid and durable HBsAg clearance, markedly reduced circulating and intrahepatic HBV DNA and RNA, and suppressed viral replication without hepatocellular injury. Vaccination elicited robust, sustained anti-HBs IgG1 and IgA responses, enhanced HBsAg-specific T- and B-cell immunity, reduced CD4 regulatory T cells, and decreased PD-1 expression on CD4 T cells. Therapeutic efficacy was strictly dependent on CD4 T cells and the CD40/CD40L signaling pathway, but independent of CD8 T cells, indicating a CD4-driven, non-cytolytic antiviral mechanism critical for HEPLISAV-B-induced HBV control. Conclusions: HEPLISAV-B effectively breaks HBV-induced immune tolerance and restores coordinated antiviral immunity through a CD4 T cell/CD40L-dependent pathway. The findings support its potential as a therapeutic vaccine in CHB patients.

title: ANTIVIRAL THERAPIES AND PUBLIC HEALTH SURVEILLANCE IN THE TREATMENT OF CHRONIC VIRAL HEPATITIS
abstract: This study is a narrative literature review that aims to critically analyze contemporary antiviral therapeutic approaches and public health surveillance models for the management of chronic viral hepatitis, specifically those caused by hepatitis B (HBV) and C (HCV) viruses. The research was conducted in the PubMed database, selecting clinical guidelines, international consensus statements, and economic evaluations published in the last five years, and analyzing the clinical, virological, and pharmacoeconomic impact of these conditions. The results demonstrate that, with regard to the treatment of hepatitis C, the use of direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) has established a highly effective model of virological cure through short-duration regimens. In contrast, in the treatment of hepatitis B, the transition from therapies with nucleoside (t)ides (NAs) to finite-duration treatment strategies and combination regimens—namely with pegylated interferon (Peg-IFN) and new-generation RNA-silencing agents—in order to achieve functional cure through sustained elimination of HBsAg. It is concluded that pharmacological innovations, while essential, need to be complemented by a restructuring of public health policies, including the expansion of population-based screening and the simplification of treatment criteria.
authors: Tarcila de Brito Lira Dal Monte Gadelha
Ana Paula Araujo Lopes da Silva
journal: International Journal of Health Management Review

title: Rare and Novel Hepatitis C Virus Genotype Subtypes and Response to Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir in A5360 (MINMON) Clinical Trial.
abstract: The introduction of potent, well-tolerated direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) has transformed hepatitis C virus (HCV) therapy and spurred global elimination efforts. However, the extensive genetic diversity of HCV may affect antiviral efficacy, particularly in low and middle-income regions where limited data currently exist. Using samples from the ACTG A5360 (MINMON) trial, which evaluated a minimal-monitoring strategy with 12 weeks of sofosbuvir/velpatasvir (SOF/VEL) across five countries, we characterized rare and novel HCV subtypes and assessed baseline resistance-associated substitutions (RASs) and treatment response. Genotype/subtype assignments were obtained by NS5B short-fragment sequencing and confirmed through next-generation and whole-genome sequencing. Among 399 participants, 389 (97.5%) were successfully genotyped; whole-genome sequencing in unresolved genotypes identified several provisional novel genotype 4 subtypes and a putative new genotype 7 subtype (7c). Despite the presence of baseline NS5A RASs, all participants with initially unsubtyped infections achieved sustained virologic response (SVR12). Reduced SVR was observed primarily among genotype 3b infections (78%), consistent with prior data linking A30K + L31M RASs to decreased NS5A inhibitor susceptibility. Overall, SOF/VEL achieved high SVR across genotypes, including rare and novel subtypes. These findings underscore both the increased recognition of global HCV genetic diversity and the robust performance of pangenotypic DAA regimens, supporting universal adoption of simplified treatment strategies, as proposed by the MINMON trial, towards HCV elimination. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03512210.

title: Erythrocyte phosphatidylserine externalization shows greater discriminatory performance than red cell distribution width for early recurrence or progression in hepatocellular carcinoma.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Red cell distribution width (RDW) is associated with adverse outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but whether this association reflects an HCC-associated erythrocyte injury phenotype remains unclear. We investigated whether phosphatidylserine (PS) externalization identifies an HCC-associated erythrocyte injury phenotype and is associated with tumor burden and early recurrence or progression. METHODS: This prospective two-center clinical study included 97 patients with newly diagnosed HCC, 30 healthy donors, 13 patients with chronic hepatitis B, and 17 patients with HBV-related cirrhosis as disease controls. Erythrocyte injury phenotypes were characterized by flow cytometry, metabolomics, and proteomics. Findings were examined in orthotopic HCC mouse models and erythrocyte-HCC co-culture systems. RESULTS: PS externalization was elevated in patients with HCC and correlated with tumor diameter, multiplicity, metastasis, and Barcelona Clinic Liver Cancer stage. HCC also showed higher PS levels than chronic hepatitis B and HBV-related cirrhosis controls. Higher PS externalization remained independently associated with early recurrence or progression within 6 months after adjustment for maximum tumor diameter, tumor number, and lymph-node and/or distant metastasis (OR = 1.382; 95% CI 1.112-1.717; P = 0.004). PS showed greater discriminatory performance than RDW-CV (AUC 0.804 versus 0.642; paired DeLong P = 0.003); bootstrap internal validation of the primary multivariable model yielded an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.780. Spatial analyses revealed progressive erythrocyte injury from peripheral blood to adjacent non-tumor tissue to primary tumor. In orthotopic HCC-bearing mice, PS externalization preceded RDW elevation. Direct co-culture with HCC cells induced glutathione depletion and oxidative membrane injury, which were attenuated by N-acetylcysteine and reproduced by glutathione synthesis inhibition. Multi-omics analyses revealed alterations in pentose phosphate pathway (PPP)-NADPH/glutathione metabolism and membrane-skeletal proteins. CONCLUSIONS: PS externalization identifies an HCC-associated erythrocyte injury phenotype and is a candidate marker for 6-month recurrence or progression. Experimental findings support a functional contribution of glutathione depletion to membrane injury, accompanied by PPP-NADPH-related metabolic and membrane-skeletal alterations.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Assisted Tools in the Diagnosis of Liver Infections: A Narrative Review
abstract: Liver infections, caused by bacterial, parasitic and viral agents, remain a major cause of global morbidity and mortality. They are diagnostically challenging because their clinical and imaging features overlap and specialist expertise is unevenly distributed. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted tools for the diagnosis, staging and risk stratification of liver infections. Machine learning, deep learning, radiomics and natural language processing have been applied across various liver infections, with multimodal models consistently outperforming single-modality approaches. Deep learning applied to ultrasound and contrast-enhanced CT achieved the strongest results, most notably in hepatic echinococcosis, while radiomics and machine learning models performed well for pathogen classification in pyogenic abscess and for fibrosis staging in schistosomiasis and hepatitis B. Evidence on AI application for amoebic liver abscess, fasciolosis, hepatic tuberculosis or cytomegalovirus hepatitis is nearly absent. Current evidence therefore supports technical feasibility rather than demonstrate clinical benefit. Major limitations impeding clinical application of AI tools include data scarcity and class imbalance, limited interpretability, retrospective single-centre designs, sparse external validation and inconsistent reporting of detailed performance metrics. Priorities include multicenter datasets from endemic, resource-limited settings, prospective validation, explainability and health-economic evaluation. Importantly, AI should be a reliable tool that support rather than replace clinician judgement.

title: Trends in Hepatitis D Virus Prevalence Among HBsAg-Positive Individuals With and Without HIV in Italy: A Converging Epidemiology.
abstract: BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Hepatitis D virus (HDV) infection has historically been more prevalent among people with HIV (PWH) due to shared transmission routes. Whether HIV status still identifies a subgroup at higher risk of HDV in contemporary settings remains unclear. METHODS: We performed two cross-sectional analyses assessing anti-HDV prevalence among HBsAg-positive PWH enrolled in the ICONA cohort in 2009-2012 and 2019-2023, compared with HIV-negative individuals from the MASTER and PITER cohorts. RESULTS: Anti-HDV prevalence among PWH declined from 19.1% to 12.5%, converging with that observed in HIV-negative individuals (12.7%). Injection drug use markedly decreased over time among PWH and remained the strongest determinant of HDV infection. In multivariable analyses, HDV seropositivity was associated with age, injection drug use, and birth outside Italy, but not with HIV infection in the contemporary period. CONCLUSION: These findings indicate that HIV infection is no longer independently associated with HDV infection in this setting and support universal HDV screening strategies.

title: Risk factors associated with prolonged treatment courses of chronic hepatitis E.
abstract: Abstract Background and aims Chronic hepatitis E virus (HEV) infection is a relevant complication in immunocompromised patients and remains therapeutically challenging due to variable response to ribavirin (RBV). We aimed to identify clinical and biochemical factors associated with prolonged or unsuccessful treatment courses. Methods In this retrospective single-center study, 41 patients with chronic HEV infection (HEV RNA detectable ≥ 12 weeks) treated between 2016 and 2024 were analyzed. Prolonged treatment (> 12 weeks), retreatment, or persistent viremia were defined as complicated treatment courses. Results The median patient age was 54 years. Ten patients (24.4%) were female. Transaminases were elevated at the time of diagnosis with a median ALT of 118 U/l and GGT of 127 U/l. Median elastography was 6.2 kPa. 4 patients died; 30/37 patients (81%) required ribavirin treatment. Out of those, HEV cure occurred after 12 weeks of ribavirin treatment in 16 patients (53.3%), whereas eleven patients (36.6%) needed longer treatment courses or retreatment. Three patients (10%) have an ongoing HEV infection. Male sex ( p = 0.03) and age > 50 years ( p = 0.04) were associated with complicated treatment courses. Both normal and high ALT levels (> 200 U/L) at baseline had poorer outcomes, and a BMI < 28 kg/m 2 was linked to prolonged viremia. Conclusion In this retrospective cohort, older age, male sex, and distinct ALT patterns were associated with complicated treatment courses. However, these exploratory findings require cautious interpretation given the limited sample size, heterogeneous patient population, and potential confounding. A subset of patients exhibits persistent infection despite therapy, underscoring the need for improved antiviral strategies and individualized management.

title: Multi-Omics Identifies Associations of Gut Roseburia Abundance and Butyrate Levels with Antiviral Responses to Entecavir Plus Interferon-α in HBV Mouse Models
abstract: Background: Individuals with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection present with gut dysbiosis. Evidence suggests that gut microbiota can affect the efficacy of anti-HBV therapy. However, limited research has comprehensively explored how gut microbiota and its related metabolites interact with HBV treatment response after antiviral treatment. Our study aims to identify an association between the dominant microbial cluster and HBV treatment response during anti-viral therapies. Methods: HBV carrier mice were utilized to assess the antiviral efficacy and peripheral and intrahepatic immune responses of entecavir (ETV) and ETV plus interferon-α (EI) therapies. We analyzed the gut microbiome, metabolome, and non-parenchymal hepatic cells transcriptome to determine the role of gut microbes and related metabolites in virological and intrahepatic immune responses to ETV and EI. Mice receiving no therapy (HBV control), ETV monotherapy, and EI therapy were used for comparison. Furthermore, we used immune cells to evaluate the effects of metabolites produced by the identified bacteria. Results: EI therapy showed a greater trend toward reducing serum HBsAg and HBeAg levels compared with ETV monotherapy, and significantly decreased intrahepatic HBcAg expression. Principal coordinates analysis revealed that gut microbes and metabolites were significantly different in the EI treatment group and the ETV and HBV groups. Notably, the relative abundance of short-chain fatty acid-producing bacteria was higher in the EI group, particularly in gut Roseburia abundance and butyrate levels. Butyrate levels were also elevated in the liver. However, whether this reflects intestinal absorption or hepatic synthesis remains undetermined. Butyrate is a potent inhibitor of histone deacetylases (HDACs), which can reduce the expression of hepatic HDAC and also suppress its activity. Hepatic HDAC1 protein levels were lower in the EI group than ETV group, consistent with the possibility that butyrate may modulate HDAC1 expression. Furthermore, EI treatment increased hepatic NKG2D+ NK cells and upregulated the NK cell-mediated cytotoxicity pathway. In vitro studies revealed that 0.5 mM butyrate enhanced the cytokine response of CD8+ T cells to HBV surface-specific antigens. Conclusions: Our multi-omics analysis reveals an association of gut Roseburia abundance and butyrate levels with improved virological responses to EI therapy. In vitro, butyrate enhanced the cytokine response of HBV-specific CD8+ T cells, suggesting a hypothesis that butyrate (but does not verify mediation of the virological responses to EI) may contribute to the antiviral response. While our multi-omics and in vitro data support a testable working hypothesis that butyrate may contribute to intrahepatic immune modulation, we acknowledge that causality is not established by this study. These results provide potential possibilities for future functional investigations of butyrate-producing microbiota as an adjunct to anti-HBV therapy.

title: Hepatitis C viral variants bear signatures of de novo CD8+ T cell and antibody pressure after spontaneous postpartum viral suppression.
abstract: Progression to chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection entails loss of HCV-specific CD4+ T cell help, emergence of viral variants that escape recognition by CD8+ T cells and neutralizing antibodies, and exhaustion of CD8+ T cells targeting remaining intact epitopes. Once chronic infection has been established, it is generally lifelong without treatment. However, in some chronically infected women, a surprising postpartum viral load decline has been linked to resurgent functional HCV-specific CD4+ helper T cells. A minority of women even spontaneously clear long-standing chronic infection postpartum. To test whether restored T cell help boosts HCV-specific CD8+ T cell or antibody responses in women with postpartum viral control, we performed serial near-full-length deep sequencing of HCV genomes to assess evolution of viral MHC class I epitopes and antibody epitopes in nine women with significant postpartum viral declines (≥ 1 log 10 at 3 mo postpartum, "controllers") and 12 with more stable levels ("noncontrollers"). Although not associated with mutations arising early postpartum, at 12 to 24 mo postpartum, viral control was strongly associated with amino acid mutations in epitopes predicted to be targeted by CD8+ T cells and neutralizing antibodies. Plasma from controllers also demonstrated a postpartum increase in neutralization of multiple HCV strains. Together, these findings support the hypothesis that postpartum viral control is mediated by CD8+ T cell and antibody pressure.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

title: TIGIT expression induces NKT-like cell hypofunction in hepatocellular carcinoma patients with high HBV load
abstract: Abstract Persistent hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection can induce chronic hepatitis B and liver cirrhosis and gradually progress to hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Particularly, a high serum HBV DNA level is a major risk factor for the development of HCC. CD3+CD56+ NKT-like cells play a pivotal role in human antiviral defense and tumor immune surveillance. Nevertheless, the mechanism underlying the immune status of NKT-like cells in HCC patients with high HBV DNA level remains to be elucidated. In this study, we demonstrated that peripheral blood NKT-like cells from HCC patients with high HBV DNA level (high-HBV HCC patients, HBV DNA > 10 4 IU/mL) displayed hypofunction, characterized by upregulated expression of the inhibitory receptor TIGIT and impaired secretion of antiviral effector cytokines. Elevated TIGIT expression on NKT-like cells is positively correlated with HBV DNA level in HCC patients. Moreover, the immune activity of TIGIT+ NKT-like cells was significantly lower than that of the TIGIT− subset. Meanwhile, we found that compared to HCC patients with low HBV DNA level (low-HBV HCC patients), the expression of CD155 (the ligand for TIGIT) on plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) was markedly upregulated in high-HBV HCC patients. Co-culture assay of NKT-like cells and pDCs showed that TIGIT blockade restored the effector function of NKT-like cells of HCC patients upon HBcAg stimulation. Taken together, our results indicate that the TIGIT pathway mediates hypofunction of NKT-like cells in high-HBV HCC patients, providing a rationale for developing novel immune checkpoint for HCC patients with high HBV load.

title: Development and validation of a LightGBM-based diagnostic model for acute-on-chronic liver failure in patients with liver cirrhosis: a multicenter retrospective study in an HBV-predominant cohort
abstract: Background Acute-on-chronic liver failure (ACLF) is a severe and often fatal complication in patients with liver cirrhosis. Because its clinical manifestations in the early stage are often masked by the chronic liver disease, timely identification and risk stratification of ACLF are critical for improving clinical outcomes. Therefore, the present study aimed to develop a model for timely identification and risk stratification of ACLF. Methods In this multicenter retrospective study, data were collected from seven tertiary hospitals in Southwest China, including 17,567 patients with cirrhosis between 2012 and 2023. Feature selection was performed using Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO) regression. Multiple machine learning algorithms, including Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM), were developed and compared for ACLF prediction. Model performance was assessed and validated using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC–ROC), area under the precision–recall curve (AUC–PR), calibration curves, and decision curve analysis. The TreeSHAP framework was applied for model interpretation. Results A total of 13,490 eligible patients with cirrhosis were included, of whom 1,250 (9.27%) developed ACLF. The cohort was randomly divided into a training set ( n = 9,758) and a test set ( n = 4,182). Among the evaluated algorithms, the LightGBM model demonstrated the best predictive performance. In the training set, the LightGBM model yielded an AUROC of 0.960, an AUPRC of 0.727, an accuracy of 0.882, a sensitivity of 0.954, a specificity of 0.875 and an F1 score of 0.593. In the test set, the corresponding values were 0.948, 0.655, 0.866, 0.912, 0.861, and 0.549, respectively. SHAP analysis identified the nine most important predictive features, ranked by their contribution to the model: international normalized ratio, total bilirubin, prealbumin, hepatitis B virus infection, alanine aminotransferase, platelet count, total bile acid, hepatic encephalopathy and alcoholic liver disease. Conclusion A LightGBM-based diagnostic model incorporating nine key clinical variables was successfully developed. This model facilitates timely identification and risk stratification of ACLF in patients with cirrhosis, which may support clinical decision-making at presentation and targeted clinical interventions.

title: Hepatitis E virus infections in immunocompromised patients.
abstract: SUMMARY Hepatitis E virus (HEV) is an important cause of viral hepatitis globally. Historically considered an acute and self-limiting illness, HEV has emerged as a significant pathogen in various immunocompromised patient groups in the last 15 years. Vulnerable patients include transplant recipients, people living with advanced HIV infection, and patients with hematological malignancies, rheumatological disorders, or autoimmune diseases. These individuals are vulnerable to chronic hepatitis and extrahepatic manifestations due to HEV. These risks are also relevant to emerging modalities of immunosuppression such as new targeted drug therapies and chimeric antigen receptor T-cell therapies. Besides unique clinical implications, immunocompromised hosts have also been at the center of new developments in the hepatitis E field on zoonotic reservoirs, transmission routes, disease models, and pathogenesis. In this review, we present a comprehensive integrative summary of the epidemiology, clinical manifestations, pathogenesis, diagnosis, and management strategies of HEV infections in immunocompromised hosts.

title: Trends in hepatitis C treatment initiation alongside changes in Medicaid policy requirements: Wisconsin, January 2015-December 2022.
abstract: Background Treatment is recommended for all persons with hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection, which substantially reduces HCV-associated morbidity and mortality. A US state Medicaid program incrementally removed policies restricting access to direct-acting antiviral (DAA) treatment, including specialist and severity requirements (2017), sobriety (2019), and prior authorization (2020). We evaluated longitudinal trends in hepatitis C treatment initiation alongside the timing of these policy changes. Objective To describe HCV treatment initiation rates concurrently with the removal of restrictive policies among a population of Medicaid recipients with recently diagnosed infection. Methods We matched public health surveillance data and Medicaid claims to identify Medicaid recipients with HCV infection during January 2015-December 2022. We defined treatment initiation as at least 1 pharmacy claim for DAAs within 6 months of hepatitis C diagnosis among persons with 6-month continuous Medicaid enrollment. We evaluated longitudinal changes in treatment rates across distinct policy periods using modified Poisson regression models adjusted for sex, race, ethnicity, and birthyear cohort. Adjusted rate ratios and 95% CIs were calculated. Results Yearly treatment ranged from 1% (among those diagnosed in 2015) to a maximum of 23% (among those diagnosed in 2020). In the multivariable model evaluating trends concurrent with policy changes, treatment initiation was 2.8 times (95% CI = 2.2-3.6) as high as baseline during the period without specialist provider and disease severity restrictions; 3.7 times (95% CI = 2.8-4.8) as high during the period without sobriety restrictions; and 5.6 times (95% CI = 4.4-7.0) as high during the period when all administrative restrictions were absent. Conclusions Overall treatment uptake remained low in this population of Medicaid beneficiaries diagnosed with hepatitis C, despite the incremental removal of policy requirements. Although relative treatment rates increased across successive policy periods, initiation peaked at just 23%. These findings suggest that although removing administrative barriers is a necessary baseline step, policy liberalization alone is insufficient to achieve hepatitis C elimination, and additional clinical and structural interventions are needed.

title: Longitudinal Surface Water Viral Surveillance Following the 2024 Extreme Flood: One-Year Monitoring in Porto Alegre, Brazil.
abstract: Extreme flood events can overwhelm sanitation infrastructure and drive the widespread dispersal of viral pathogens into aquatic environments. In May 2024, Porto Alegre (southern Brazil) experienced an unprecedented flood that caused record-breaking overflow of the Guaíba hydrological system and prolonged urban inundation. Here we report a one-year longitudinal environmental viral surveillance study, comprising seven campaigns between May 2024 and April 2025. Surface waters were analyzed by RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2, norovirus genogroups I and II, hepatitis A virus (HAV) and hepatitis E virus (HEV). All five targets were detected simultaneously during the flood peak, reflecting widespread contamination possibly driven by sewage overflow and multi-site infrastructure failure. Thereafter, the number of targets detected per campaign was lower and fluctuating (two to four), tracing a transition from an initial multi-pathogen contamination pulse observed during the flood peak to persistent detection of viral genomic material in surface waters. SARS-CoV-2 was detected in every campaign, in a minority of sites in all campaigns except the last (C7, 14/22, 63.6%), where both detection frequency and viral load increased significantly (p < 0.001 for both; median Ct 29.7 versus 36.8). HEV was detected only at the flood peak; norovirus GII was detected intermittently up to C6, without a significant temporal pattern (p = 0.13); and norovirus GI was absent between C2 and C5, reappearing in C6 and C7. HAV detection increased significantly over the monitoring period (Cochran-Armitage p < 0.0005), temporally coincident with an officially declared hepatitis A outbreak. These findings demonstrate the value of longitudinal, multi-target environmental surveillance for capturing both the acute virological impact of extreme flooding and the persistent contamination dynamics that follow, pointing to chronic vulnerabilities in urban wastewater infrastructure that outlast the emergency.

source_records.title: Longitudinal Surface Water Viral Surveillance Following the 2024 Extreme Flood: One-Year Monitoring in Porto Alegre, Brazil
source_records.abstract: Extreme flood events can overwhelm sanitation infrastructure and drive the widespread dispersal of viral pathogens into aquatic environments. In May 2024, Porto Alegre (southern Brazil) experienced an unprecedented flood that caused record-breaking overflow of the Guaíba hydrological system and prolonged urban inundation. Here we report a one-year longitudinal environmental viral surveillance study, comprising seven campaigns between May 2024 and April 2025. Surface waters were analyzed by RT-qPCR for SARS-CoV-2, norovirus genogroups I and II, hepatitis A virus (HAV) and hepatitis E virus (HEV). All five targets were detected simultaneously during the flood peak, reflecting widespread contamination possibly driven by sewage overflow and multi-site infrastructure failure. Thereafter, the number of targets detected per campaign was lower and fluctuating (two to four), tracing a transition from an initial multi-pathogen contamination pulse observed during the flood peak to persistent detection of viral genomic material in surface waters. SARS-CoV-2 was detected in every campaign, in a minority of sites in all campaigns except the last (C7, 14/22, 63.6%), where both detection frequency and viral load increased significantly (p < 0.001 for both; median Ct 29.7 versus 36.8). HEV was detected only at the flood peak; norovirus GII was detected intermittently up to C6, without a significant temporal pattern (p = 0.13); and norovirus GI was absent between C2 and C5, reappearing in C6 and C7. HAV detection increased significantly over the monitoring period (Cochran-Armitage p < 0.0005), temporally coincident with an officially declared hepatitis A outbreak. These findings demonstrate the value of longitudinal, multi-target environmental surveillance for capturing both the acute virological impact of extreme flooding and the persistent contamination dynamics that follow, pointing to chronic vulnerabilities in urban wastewater infrastructure that outlast the emergency.

title: Complete response to fourth-line nivolumab in metastatic hepatocellular carcinoma: A case report
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is an important cause of cancer-related mortality, and systemic therapies have historically provided only limited benefit. While immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have reshaped treatment strategies in HCC, durable complete responses with nivolumab monotherapy are rare. We describe a 71-year-old male with HCC related to hepatitis B virus (HBV) who failed multiple systemic therapies including capecitabine, sorafenib, and regorafenib. Nivolumab was initiated in December 2019, and complete remission was achieved within three months of treatment. The patient maintained a complete response for over six years without significant immune-related toxicity. This case demonstrates the potential of achieving exceptional and durable efficacy with nivolumab monotherapy in advanced HCC, even in patients previously treated with several lines of systemic treatment.

title: Adherence to Adult Vaccination After Family Physician Recommendation: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study in Primary Care
abstract: Objective: To determine adherence to family physician-recommended adult vaccines in primary care and whether it differed by sex, age, or the type and number of vaccines. Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included adults recommended one or more risk-based vaccines at 2 family medicine units in Güngören, İstanbul, Türkiye, between June and August 2022. Tetanus vaccination for trauma or pregnancy and COVID-19 vaccination were excluded. Data were obtained from the Family Medicine Information System; doses recorded after the recommendation were counted up to data extraction in July-August 2023. Adherence was classified as full (at least 1 dose of every recommended vaccine), partial, or no recorded uptake. Chi-square tests and exploratory Firth logistic regression were used. Results: The 152 patients had a mean age of 58.7 years; 57.2% were women. Tetanus-diphtheria (Td) was recommended to 67.8% of patients, 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV13) to 61.8%, 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23) to 26.3%, hepatitis B to 13.8%, and other vaccines to 2.0%. Administration rates were 79.6% for Td, 85.1% for PCV13, 85.0% for PPSV23, and 76.2% for hepatitis B. Overall, 120 patients (78.9%; 95% CI, 71.8%-84.7%) were fully adherent, 6 (3.9%) partially adherent, and 26 (17.1%) had no recorded uptake. No significant differences were detected by sex, age group, or number of vaccines. Conclusion: At least 1 dose of every recommended vaccine was recorded for most adults recommended risk-based vaccines by their family physician. Without a comparison group, these findings describe uptake after a recommendation, not the effect of the recommendation.

title: Hepatitis C Micro-Elimination Through Patient Navigation of Individuals Experiencing Elevated Risk in a Mid-Atlantic Regional Healthcare System in 2022 and 2023: A Cohort Study.
abstract: ABSTRACT Background and Aims Hepatitis C virus (HCV) disproportionately impacts persons with substance use and mental health disorders. Micro‐elimination projects selectively foster diagnosis, treatment and reinfection of high priority demographic groups. A small‐scale, peer navigation focused micro‐elimination project was launched at a regional multidisciplinary and multispecialty health system in the Mid‐Atlantic to facilitate treatment engagement for high‐risk individuals. Methods The program used electronic medical record (EMR) periodic surveillance and navigation of individuals diagnosed with HCV and either not engaged, or not completed, treatment, as well as those needing additional testing (for either sustained virologic response or high‐risk re‐testing). Specialist appointments and referrals for associated behavioral health interventions were provided. Historical propensity score matched controls were utilized to provide a comparator population. Results Between April 2022 and July 2023, 115 persons were navigated, including 78 persons without a prior specialist appointment (New Patients), 15 persons previously engaged with a specialist but not completing treatment, and 22 patients needing additional testing. Among New Patients, 52.6% of patients attended treatment appointments, 28.2% started treatment, and 14.1% had a confirmed undetectable HCV test. Compared to historical matched controls, persons navigated were almost twice as likely to attend an appointment (HR: 1.96 [1.18–3.23], p = 0.008), and nearly three times more likely to start treatment (HR: 2.86 [1.41–5.79], p = 0.003). The median time from navigation to an appointment for New Patients was 71 days, and 143 days until starting treatment. Conclusions A small‐scale, peer‐navigation focused micro‐navigation program successfully engaged patients but had mixed success in successfully navigating the care cascade. Despite navigation and consistent engagement, nearly half of patients dropped off at each step of the care cascade. Compared to historical controls, patients were more likely to make appointments and initiate treatment. Future efforts should be targeted at reducing times for specialist appointments and expanding treatment at diagnosis location.

title: Case Report: Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome caused by Seoul orthohantavirus mimicking severe acute pancreatitis: dynamic imaging evolution and pathogen confirmation by mNGS
abstract: Background Hemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) is a zoonotic disease caused by orthohantaviruses, characterized by fever, thrombocytopenia, renal impairment, and capillary leak syndrome. Its atypical presentations can closely mimic acute pancreatitis (AP), posing substantial diagnostic challenges. Case presentation A 33-year-old man presented with fever, vomiting, and watery diarrhea. Initial computed tomography (CT) revealed peripancreatic and perirenal exudation suggestive of severe acute pancreatitis. He already had profound thrombocytopenia on admission (nadir 29 × 109/L), progressive renal impairment, hematuria, and proteinuria, without typical pancreatitis risk factors or elevated pancreatic enzymes. Contrast-enhanced CT demonstrated progressive retroperitoneal exudation with relatively mild pancreatic parenchymal changes and newly developed bilateral pleural effusion. Whole-blood metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) detected high-copy Seoul orthohantavirus, with concurrent hepatitis B virus. The patient recovered fully with supportive care, intravenous immunoglobulin, and symptomatic treatment; pre-discharge ultrasound showed normal pancreatic morphology. Conclusion Seoul orthohantavirus infection can closely mimic severe acute pancreatitis clinically and radiologically. Disproportionate thrombocytopenia, renal involvement, and progressive retroperitoneal exudation with preserved pancreatic parenchyma are key diagnostic clues, and mNGS enables early definitive pathogen confirmation, facilitating appropriate management.

title: Association Between Hepatitis C Virus Infection and Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: Background: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection has been associated with cardiovascular disease, but its relationship with coronary artery disease (CAD) remains uncertain. Methods: This systematic review included observational studies reporting adjusted effect estimates for CAD outcomes among HCV-infected and HCV-uninfected adults. Adjusted hazard ratios, risk ratios, and odds ratios were combined on the logarithmic scale using a random-effects model and are presented as a summary relative association estimate with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Prespecified subgroup analyses were performed by study design, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection status, and CAD outcome type; meta-regression evaluated follow-up duration, mean age, and the proportion of male participants. Results: Twenty-one studies were included, representing diverse populations including veterans, people living with HIV, dialysis patients, and community-based cohorts. Fifteen studies contributed adjusted estimates to the quantitative synthesis. HCV infection was associated with a modest increase in the pooled relative estimate for CAD (summary estimate 1.21; 95% CI, 1.05–1.40; P = 0.007), with substantial heterogeneity (I2 = 72.1%). The association was statistically significant in cohort studies and in both HIV-specific and non-HIV-specific subgroups, although the HIV-specific subgroup was based on four studies. The myocardial infarction (MI)-specific subgroup was not statistically significant, whereas studies using broader CAD outcomes showed a significant association. Conclusions: Chronic HCV infection was associated with a modest increase in the pooled relative estimate for CAD. However, substantial heterogeneity, differences in endpoint definitions and populations, residual confounding, and the combination of different effect measures limit causal interpretation and make the clinical importance uncertain. The nonsignificant MI-specific analysis further supports a cautious interpretation. These findings do not establish a cardiovascular benefit of antiviral therapy; prospective studies with standardized CAD endpoints and detailed data on renal disease, antiviral exposure, and lipid-lowering therapy are needed.

title: Crowder-specific modulation of hepatitis C virus NS3/4A protease activity and local structural dynamics.
abstract: Macromolecular crowding modulates enzyme behavior in crowder- and protein-specific ways, yet its impact on viral proteases, which are often key therapeutic targets, remains unclear. Here, we investigated the hepatitis C virus NS3/4A protease under increasing concentrations of polyethylene glycols (PEGs), ficoll, dextran, and lysozyme using fluorescence-based assays to examine enzyme kinetics, local Trp environments, thermal stability, and rotational restriction of the fluorescent probe in the surrounding medium. PEGs reduced catalytic activity while leaving substrate binding either unaffected or slightly enhanced. These effects were accompanied by a moderate tryptophan fluorescence spectral narrowing, consistent with reduced heterogeneity in local conformational environments. In contrast, ficoll enhanced catalytic efficiency despite stronger fluorescence quenching, indicating local structural changes that favored catalysis. Dextran and lysozyme inhibited protease activity through distinct kinetic patterns, likely reflecting differences in their size, shape, and chemical properties. Thermal analysis revealed crowder-specific local structural changes in NS3/4A without global unfolding up to 65°C, with differences in local stability and flexibility corroborating the observed kinetic effects. Changes in the rotational restriction of the fluorescent probe further indicated that generalized restriction of molecular motion alone could not explain the effects of crowding on NS3/4A. These findings demonstrate that macromolecular crowding modulates NS3/4A catalysis through crowder-specific effects on local structure.
